question.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=\sqrt{x-4}.$ Notice that 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(4) & =\sqrt{4-4} \\  & =\sqrt{0} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's sketch the graph of $y=f(x):$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14253135/assets/4c434365084b3123c313d5de1ddd0692e1658b6fcc6b7c03869cb2cebf94253e.png)

From the graph, we notice that for the left-hand limit, we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to {4}^{-}}f(x)=\text{DNE}
$$

For the right-hand limit, we have:

$$
{lim}_{x\to {4}^{+}}f(x)=0
$$

Since the two limits are not equal, we conclude that

$$
{lim}_{x\to 4}f(x)=\text{DNE}.
$$
